comment: Numeric ratchet manifest (DR-27a). Two arrays, two directions, one mechanism — tests/guards/numeric-floor-manifest.test.ts enforces both. `floors` entries may RISE, never fall. `ceilings` entries may be LOWERED, never raised: a budget or a maximum that can be raised to fit whatever the artifact grew into is not a budget, it asserts that the current size is the current size. Each entry pins a value AND the number of sites spelling it: the guard requires at least `occurrences` matches of `pattern` in `sourceFile`, so moving one site out of several is caught. New entries are allowed in either array; move `floor`/`ceiling`, `pattern` and `occurrences` together, and only in the permitted direction. Equality baselines (the GIT_MD_* / SKILL_* / TOTAL_* constants in tests/goldens/github-status-lines.test.ts) ratchet in neither direction and are not registered here.

floors.description: Number of compiled MDS host commands in dist/commands/ (MDS_COMMAND_HOSTS). The discovery assertion is a set-equality against tests/fixtures/mds-manifest.ts and this floor is that manifest's length, asserted alongside the set: the set says WHICH hosts, the floor says the roster may not shrink behind it. The pattern names its RECEIVER because partial-count in the same file now pins the same number: two entries sharing one bare pattern have no per-entry accounting, and the decrement probe of each would keep finding the other's site.

Number of .mds partial files anywhere under src/ (ALL_MDS_PARTIALS = MDS_PARTIALS under src/assets/commands/_partials/, plus MDS_REFERENCE_PARTIALS elsewhere: _common.mds and _steps.mds under src/assets/mds/tracker/). The discovery assertion is a set-equality against tests/fixtures/mds-manifest.ts over a repo-wide walk that classifies by the build's own rule -- no output-dir: key -- so a partial parked outside _partials/ is named rather than merely counted; this floor is its length. Floors rise with the roster, never fall — a partial deleted rather than inlined takes its callers with it silently.

DIST_FILES count = COMMAND_HOSTS (14), one compiled file per command host. Five sites spell it, including the `<!-- devflow:` marker negative guard, which asserts both the built file count and its own distFilesScanned counter — the value is one number and the occurrence count is what stops one site drifting out of the set.

Minimum timeout in ms for the slow shell-exec tests that spawn scripts/build-mds.ts. Three sites, all direct negative-path spawns in this file: two dest-safety refusals and the ignored-dir walk. Every other isolated MDS build in this file routes through runMdsBuild(), directly (the TP-12 reference-module probes) or through buildCommittedTree(); its timeout is pinned by the mds-build-spawn-timeout-ms entry below.

Minimum timeout in ms for runMdsBuild() — the one spawn site every isolated MDS build in tests/build-mds.test.ts routes through, except the three direct spawns pinned by slow-test-timeout-ms. Its callers are buildCommittedTree() and the TP-12 reference-module probes. Same floor as slow-test-timeout-ms, in the file the sites moved to.
Minimum number of subagent_type literal sites across dist+scripts corpus (currently ~66+)
Minimum number of DEVFLOW_PLUGINS registry entries

Language focuses /code-review's stamp paragraph names, each held to a canonical skill. Compiled commands name no skill by install path (D-LANGUAGE-FOCUS-STAMP): the stamp paragraph is the one place a command lists the language skills, so this count is what keeps the Format 3 compiled-command check from passing on an empty set.

D11 forward guard: posting ops (--body-file / -F body=@) that must reference Comment-sink scrub (D11), counted over the sink corpus gitAgentSinkCorpus() returns -- the resolved Git agent UNIONED with dist/skills/git/references/*.md, sliced in extractOpSection mode 'union' [DR-18]. The union is load-bearing: posting mechanics live in the generated references, so a git.md-only count would drop below the floor for reasons that are not a regression. 9 since #363 (PR4) added update-pr-evidence, which edits the PR body and posts the evidence comment from its PR-host reference. Operations indexed from git.md by the seam test's op→section map [DR-24]. 16 since #363 (PR4) declared update-pr-evidence; 17 since #364 (PR5) declared associate-release; git.md declares 20 operations.

Operations with at least one live caller fence. Directions 1 and 2 iterate this map; if it empties, both pass vacuously (the defect this floor exists to make loud). 14 since #363 (PR4): /implement's Phase 10b spawn gave update-pr-evidence its caller fence. KEYS in issue_capture_contract() checked by the seam test's producer direction. Six: the three original keys plus ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_PR_LINK and ISSUE_BRANCH_TOKEN, whose producers are the `### Handoff Values` block setup-task and fetch-issue emit. ISSUE_URL has no producer in git.md and is deliberately out. The 60 000-character body cap, asserted at 7 sites in tests/git-agent.test.ts: the manage-debt archive threshold, the post-wave-report cap, each summary op's positive union assertion plus its known-bad probe that the literal is NOT reachable once the PR-host tree is dropped (both summary operations' compose steps live in the PR-host references), and the containment negative arm's in-scope witness that its scanned surface reaches the compose templates. The pattern is a substring of the negated form too, which is why the probes count; lowering the cap at any one site is caught.

AC-0.10 containment guard (issue-body): ops wrapping remote issue content in <untrusted-issue-body> — setup-task, fetch-issue, fetch-issues-batch. The pattern names this entry's id so it matches ONE site: the sibling containment-external-thread-floor pins the same value 3 in the same file, and a bare toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3) at occurrences 2 is satisfied by the pair jointly, each entry's count met by the OTHER entry's assertion with neither site individually accounted for.

AC-0.10 containment guard (external-thread): ops carrying <external-thread> for review thread bodies — fetch-review-threads, post-resolution-summary, post-wave-report. Pattern narrowed to this entry's own site for the reason recorded on the sibling containment-issue-body-floor entry above: two entries sharing one pattern in one file have no per-entry accounting.

BUILD/TARBALL SCOPE: the manifest the build EMITS, which is every provider plus the provider-independent trees. Since #393 every install carries this whole manifest (installed-reference-count-{github,provider} pin the install side at the same 47). 47 = 11 GitHub ops + 11 Jira ops + 11 Linear ops (the SAME TRACKER_OPS roster, which is what makes file-set parity structural) + 8 PR-host ops (PR_HOST_OPS, under no provider: pull requests stay on GitHub whatever the tracker is) + 4 cross-cutting documents + the tool-call contract, whose generation gate the first tool-call provider opens + the tracker contract tracker/_contract.md, which is ungated (#425; 47 until then, 44 until #364, PR5, added associate-release to the roster). #451 (D-OP-ONE-REF) folded pr/ensure-pr-ready.md into the three per-provider ensure-pr-ready files, so the manifest fell from 48 to 47 by that one file and no operation lost a reference; every other count in this sum is unchanged. Two sites — the manifest shape assertion and the 0644 normalisation's installed-file count. A manifest short enough to enumerate by hand makes every convergence assertion vacuous (GAP-42), which is the same reason MIN_VARIANT_PAIRS exists. A floor may only rise, and here it rises by a whole module at a time. LOWERED 48 -> 47 by #451 (a deliberate exception to "a floor may only rise"): the build no longer emits references/pr/ensure-pr-ready.md (ensure-pr-ready is a tracker operation with one reference per provider, D-OP-ONE-REF), so the manifest it counts lost that one file and no operation lost a reference. Old value 48; accepted by the user 2026-10-12 as a retire-and-re-register of the count.

D-LINK-FLOOR (#448): PR-opening Git spawns that pass ISSUE_PR_LINK: themselves. One: /implement's Phase 9 ensure-pr-ready spawn, the only consumer of the captured link now that no Code spawn opens a PR (an exact-0 guard holds ISSUE_NUMBER, ISSUE_PR_LINK and PR_EXCEPTIONS out of every Code spawn). It replaces issue-pr-link-forwarding-sites (15 Code-agent spawn sites), whose relation ran over spawns that no longer carry the key. The relational guard -- a workflow that captures ISSUE_PR_LINK forwards it to its PR-opening Git spawn, /dynamic-build through PR_WAVE_BLOCK -- is vacuous over an empty set of spawns, so this count is its non-vacuity floor and may only rise.

BUILD/TARBALL SCOPE: prefix-shippability clause (i) — the tarball must carry every file the reference overlay converges to. The floor keeps the packed-set assertion non-vacuous if the manifest is ever narrowed. It pins the same manifest as generated-reference-manifest-size at the OTHER sink, and the two must move together, or a module could ship un-packed. LOWERED 48 -> 47 by #451 (a deliberate exception to "a floor may only rise"): the build no longer emits references/pr/ensure-pr-ready.md (ensure-pr-ready is a tracker operation with one reference per provider, D-OP-ONE-REF), so the manifest it counts lost that one file and no operation lost a reference. Old value 48; accepted by the user 2026-10-12 as a retire-and-re-register of the count.

Total `**Process:**` / `### Process` blocks in the tracker corpus (dist/agents/git.md + the generated reference tree). The corpus split is asserted by provenance as well as by count: since #451 (D-OP-ONE-REF) the agent body declares no operation, so every block is in the generated tree and a block found in git.md is itself a failure. 42 = 1 learn-conventions + 33 provider blocks (eleven per-op references for each of the three providers) + 8 PR-host blocks. It was 63 while git.md carried twenty `**Process:**` labels of its own and pr/ensure-pr-ready.md was a ninth PR-host file; those twenty-one blocks left with the operation text, whose steps are the `### Process` blocks counted here. A provider adds its whole roster at once, so the floor moves by a module rather than by a file. LOWERED 63 -> 42 by #451 (a deliberate exception to "a floor may only rise"): the agent's twenty `**Process:**` blocks and pr/ensure-pr-ready.md's block left with the operation text they labelled (D-OP-ONE-REF); the steps are the `### Process` blocks counted here, and none of them was removed. Old value 63; accepted by the user 2026-10-12 as a retire-and-re-register of the count.

Minimum characters a generated tracker reference must carry, owned by tests/tracker/reference-floor.ts and imported by the three suites that measure that shape one step apart: reference-reachability.test.ts (the GitHub tree), linear-module.test.ts (the Linear tree) and jira-module.test.ts (the Jira tree plus the `@define` body the generator reads). One owner because a number spelled at each site can drift at one of them while every other site and a presence-only guard stay green. Registered as a FLOOR, not a ceiling: every assertion reading it is `content.length < MIN_REFERENCE_CHARS` → problem, so raising it makes all three suites stricter, while LOWERING it is the weakening move — it re-admits the shape the constant exists to catch, a reference that kept its heading and lost its body. Its own JSDoc names it a floor.

Column-0 `## ` lines the live generated reference tree must carry INSIDE a code fence, so the fence-aware structure guard's absence assertion is exercised against real fenced headings rather than a corpus that has none. Today: manage-debt.md's `## Items` (1) plus ensure-traceable-issue.md's heredoc and D3-template headings (6). Lowering it re-admits a corpus in which fence-awareness is proven only by the synthetic probes in tests/guards/agent-source-resolver.test.ts.

Rows HOSTILE_PAYLOADS must carry — seven register payloads, each targeting a different sink (command substitution in two spellings, flag injection, line injection, size, credential-in-URL, query-operator escape), plus the two identity payloads that are the only rows exercising `## Assignee`'s second prohibition. Registered as a FLOOR because the payload grid grades every row against every schema cell: a row ADDED widens the evidence and must never cost a suite failure, while a row REMOVED narrows the sinks the grid covers with nothing else reporting it. Spelled as an exact count it was the ratchet inverted — adding a payload, the thing a reviewer most wants a contributor to do, failed the suite.

Rows HOSTILE_REFS must carry — shell separator, command substitution, both flag-injection spellings, path traversal, size, the zero-numbered key an unanchored digit class admits, and whitespace. Every pinned grammar in PROVIDER_REF_GRAMMARS is driven over the whole table, so one row added widens the corpus for every provider at once and one removed silently narrows it for all of them. A FLOOR for the same reason as min-hostile-payloads.

Distinct devflow: skill references across the widened closure corpus (dist/commands + agent sources + skill bodies incl. references/). Non-vacuity floor for the bidirectional requires: guard — a scanner that stopped matching would make both arms pass over an empty corpus. Measured 2026-09-19: 200 files, 297 sites, 44 distinct. LOWERED 44 -> 41 by #449 (a deliberate exception to "a floor may only rise"): the Code variants took the Step 0 table and the DOMAIN input out of the Code prompt (D-NO-RUNTIME-SKILLS), and the three skill names boundary-validation, dependency-research and patterns appeared only in that deleted Step 0 and DOMAIN text of the Code agent, so they left the corpus with it and no other reference was removed. Old value 44; accepted by the user 2026-10-12.

Old value 48; accepted by the user 2026-10-12 as a retire-and-re-register of the count.

Since #393 (PR6, D-INSTALL-ALL-PROVIDERS) the install is no longer a function of the machine's selection, so this floor pins the same shared constant as installed-reference-count-github (INSTALLED_REFS) — the two ids are kept, never deleted, and both rose to the build's 47. History: 32 at the PR-host tree (2026-09-22); 34 since #363; 36 since #364; 47 since #393; 48 since #425 (tracker/_contract.md); 47 since #451 (pr/ensure-pr-ready.md folded into the per-provider ensure-pr-ready files, D-OP-ONE-REF). LOWERED 48 -> 47 by #451 (a deliberate exception to "a floor may only rise"): the build no longer emits references/pr/ensure-pr-ready.md (ensure-pr-ready is a tracker operation with one reference per provider, D-OP-ONE-REF), so the manifest it counts lost that one file and no operation lost a reference. Old value 48; accepted by the user 2026-10-12 as a retire-and-re-register of the count.

Reference files a COMPLIANCE-OFF install carries (#648, AC-49). installed-reference-count-github and installed-reference-count-provider stay on the compliance-ON install at 47. The compliance-off install omits the 16 posting operation files (4 pr/ files and 12 tracker files) and the publication-gate document, so 30 = 47 - 17, measured 2026-10-28 from installedReferenceManifest({ compliance: false }). AC-0.6b: REQUIRED_OPS detected as doing remote I/O, read from each operation's single reference for the GitHub provider — the file a spawn is told to read, holding the operation's Input, degradation notes, Output and steps. Replaces a bare `> 0` non-vacuity check, which one detected op satisfies and which therefore cannot tell a corpus narrowing from a real removal. Zero headroom at 16 (14 + #363's update-pr-evidence + #364's associate-release). The D4 evidence half of the same guard reads the same references, so both halves share one corpus: an operation's degradation notes sit in the reference a spawn loads to run it, and a read narrowed to git.md alone would drop every op whose remote-I/O indicators live in its reference.

Rows in the write-set fence table (FENCE_ROWS, D-WRITE-SET-FENCE, #406 item 19): one per CLI toggle action plus the state-clearing and read-only actions beside them, each walked before and after against its allowlist. The coverage tests hold the table to the CLI's own --help roster and every --enable/--disable/--set a command defines, so a row can only leave by an UNFENCED_* reason; this floor stops the table shrinking behind them. Floors rise, never fall.
Distinct top-level commands with at least one write-set fence row (every registered command except init and uninstall, whose write sets are the install-snapshot goldens). Floors rise, never fall.

Locations `devflow init` is run from in the location-invariance matrix (D-INIT-LOCATION-INVARIANCE, #406 item 19): repo root, subdirectory, linked worktree, non-git directory, a repository path with a space, a symlinked HOME and a repository rooted at HOME. Each must install the identical machine side and write per-repository files only at the checkout toplevel. Floors rise, never fall.

Distinct agent types the no-hardcoded-model guard (D-SPAWN-NO-MODEL) must read out of Agent( argument lists across src/assets/{commands,agents,skills,mds} and dist/{commands,agents}. Measured 16 when the guard was added; the Fix spawns raised it to 17 (Refactor is spawned only by the orchestrator charter, which the scan does not read). A parser that stops finding spawns, or stops reading their arguments, would pass the model scan vacuously, so the count is its liveness proof. It counts types, not sites: consolidating or dropping a spawn lowers the site count but not the type count, which falls only when no prompt spawns an agent at all. Floors rise, never fall.

Agent bodies that carry a pinned `**Gate ownership:**` row (D-GATE-OWNERSHIP): Code, Fix, Refactor, Polish, Evaluate, Harden, Test and Validate. The guard pins each row's text, so a row cannot be dropped or reworded quietly; this floor stops the table shrinking behind it. Floors rise, never fall.

Roster agents that carry a `Report cap:` line (D-REPORT-CAP): the union of the plugin `agents` arrays, less `curate` and `tracker` (hook-spawned). The guard derives the roster rather than listing it and requires an exempt-field record for each member; this floor stops the derivation quietly returning fewer agents. The Git agent split (#425) removed the `git` exclusion and raised it from 14 to 15; the Explore override raised it to 16; the Fix and Refactor variants raised it to 18. Floors rise, never fall.

Dynamic-build prompt sites that name the Running commands block instead of prescribing a procedure (D-FOREGROUND-RUN): the Code implementation prompt, both Gate 1 Validate prompts, the Validate re-run after a Gate 1 fix in each pass, the Fix prompt after Gate 2, the scenario fix prompt, the review-batch fix prompt, the Test prompt and the post-merge Validate. The guard requires each site's quoted text exactly once in the source and in the compiled command; this floor stops the list shrinking behind it. Floors rise, never fall.

The install removes such a file with no backup, so the list only grows; a blanket rename that rewrites a name here drops the count and fails this floor.

Command names in tests/fixtures/released-shipped-names.ts: the commands that releases 0.1.0 to 3.9.0 installed (29). A release cannot be un-shipped, so the fixture is extended and never cut. It is the reference for the delete-list soundness guard: a shorter fixture would let a never-released name onto a delete list.
Agent names in tests/fixtures/released-shipped-names.ts: the agents that releases 0.1.0 to 3.9.0 installed (55). Extended, never cut.
Rule names in tests/fixtures/released-shipped-names.ts: the rules that releases 0.1.0 to 3.9.0 installed (15). Extended, never cut.
Skill folder names in tests/fixtures/released-shipped-names.ts: the skill folders that releases 0.1.0 to 3.9.0 installed, bare and devflow:-prefixed (84). Extended, never cut.

Bare legacy skill names with an entry in src/targets/claude-code/legacy-skill-hashes.ts (39 at 3.9.0): the bare names of the legacy skill list that releases 0.6.1 to 1.8.3 installed. A name without an entry is never moved by init, so a lost name leaves a devflow-made folder in the shared skills folder. The table only grows.

Released SKILL.md hashes in src/targets/claude-code/legacy-skill-hashes.ts, summed over the bare names (64 at 3.9.0). A lost hash makes init keep a folder that devflow made, with an edit-free SKILL.md of that release. The table only grows.

Skill folders with a file listing in tests/fixtures/released-shipped-names.ts (84, one per released skill folder). The listing is what the soundness guard checks the skillFiles delete list against. Extended, never cut.

ceilings.description: THE git.md ceiling — the one gate on dist/agents/git.md, the always-loaded half of the tracker contract/mechanics split and a term every loaded-set row below carries. Re-derived by #376 as a measured 44_163 ch plus the 80 ch general headroom, after the series close-out cut git.md by a net 94 ch. #365 (PR6), the last PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357, had closed the reservation ledger (its git.md delta was -70 ch) and set every git.md-carrying row to min(previous ceiling, measured + 80), 80 being the headroom the rows carried before the series began (82/77/73/90 ch at 5020e06). The headroom is not a reservation: any addition funds itself with a cut. The measurement follows #326's move of the PR-host operations' bodies into references/pr/{op}.md and #358's moves of non-contract text into the references each operation already loads, plus the condensed ## Principles, then #359's and #360's fixes, #362's mechanism inputs and #363's test-plan evidence op, merge-readiness evidence and CI-status fix, #364's trace map, traceability exceptions and associate-release op, #365's ensure-pr-ready caller-block inputs, and #376's close-out. No per-component decomposition of any cut is recorded — three successive re-derivations of such components disagreed once already — so measure the artifact instead: npm run build && node -e "process.stdout.write(String(require('fs').readFileSync('dist/agents/git.md','utf8').length))". May be LOWERED, never raised: a budget raised to fit the artifact is not a budget, it asserts that the current size is the current size. #393 (PR6 of epic #387) moved the Git agent's provider resolution onto the settings line and retired the mechanics-unavailable rule: git.md measured 43_832 (net -315 ch), so the ceiling fell to min(44_243, 43_832 + 80) = 43_912. #425 (the Git agent split) re-derived it downward to min(43_912, 35_474 + 80) = 35_554: the provider resolution and the tracker input contract moved into tracker/_contract.md, which a spawn reads only when it runs a tracker operation, and the provider-neutral step text of the tracker operations moved into the per-provider references; the Output section with its report cap, and the frontmatter effort and denylist, were paid for out of that cut. #445 (part 2, the Git and Tracker tool allowlists) lowered it by exactly the 251 ch the frontmatter cut took out of git.md (a 17-name denylist became a one-line allowlist): 35_554 to 35_303, the digest commit's net +2 ch on git.md leaving the headroom at 78, from 80. Re-derived by #451 (D-OP-ONE-REF, D-OP-CONTRACT-ONCE) from a measured 10_743 ch plus the 80 ch general headroom, giving 10_823: every operation's Input, degradation notes, Output template and steps left the agent for the one reference that operation loads, so the agent now holds only the shared rules, the loading table and the routing table (target ≤ 12_000 ch). The next content addition to git.mds must fund itself with a cut elsewhere in git.mds. #712 (lean Git agent) re-derived it from a measured 10_144 ch plus the 80 ch headroom: 10_224.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn under the JIRA provider — its own row, never folded into budget-loaded-set. The GitHub row keeps bytes(tracker/_mcp.md) = 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, so pricing a provider that DOES load the contract on that row would bill every GitHub user for bytes they never receive (GAP-02), and would do it by raising a ratcheted ceiling. Re-derived by #376 as a measured 75_264 (shape '2-jira. per-op split, jira path', after the close-out's net -94 ch git.md cut) plus the 80 ch general headroom. #376 changed the FORMULA, not the headroom: the row dropped its double-counted largest-file term (D-LOADED-SET-ONE-SPAWN) and now prices every in-spawn reference hop (D-BODY-HOP-CLOSURE), so its worst spawn is setup-task plus the ensure-traceable-issue mechanics its step 1c loads under ISSUE_REQUIRED. #365 (PR6), the last PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357, had closed the reservation ledger and set every git.md-carrying row to min(previous ceiling, measured + 80), 80 being the headroom the rows carried before the series began (82/77/73/90 ch at 5020e06). The headroom is not a reservation: any addition funds itself with a cut. git.md growth lands in every loaded-set row, so this row carries the same headroom. Re-measure rather than trust a figure restated here: npm run build && npx vitest run tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints every row. Trimming references/tracker/_mcp.md is the sanctioned first response to this row going red (contract prose, and the single largest term this row adds over the GitHub one), condensing the jira mechanics the second; neither is 'give the provider more room'. budget-loaded-set-linear is the sibling row; a registered MCP-backed provider with no such entry fails a named arm in the same file. LOWERED, NEVER RAISED. #393 re-derived it to min(75_344, 74_977 + 80) = 75_057: git.md -315 ch, the Jira site rung +28 ch (the settings SITE ahead of ## Project). #423 (the skills diet) re-derived it downward to min(75_057, 73_255 + 80) = 73_335, the same two preloaded-skill cuts as the GitHub row. #425 (the Git agent split) re-derived it downward to min(73_335, 72_715 + 80) = 72_795: the same git.md cut, with tracker/_contract.md billed once per spawn beside the tool-call contract. #445 (part 2, the Git and Tracker tool allowlists) lowered it by exactly the 251 ch the frontmatter cut took out of git.md (a 17-name denylist became a one-line allowlist): 72_795 to 72_544, the digest commit's net +2 ch on git.md leaving the headroom at 56, from 58. Re-derived by #451 from a measured 51_835 ch, then by #448 from a measured 51_833 ch plus the 80 ch general headroom: 51_913. PR creation moved into ensure-pr-ready (D-PR-BY-GIT), which stays under the worst op, so the row did not move.
